Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Role defination, key responsibilities etc.: 01 -Summarise your understanding of the Student Champion role, its responsibilities, boundaries and collaboration with other support roles, and note any questions you would like to discuss with the SC Team Leader.

2. Case Studies: 01 & 02 - Respond to the second set of case studies covering confidentiality, escalation and boundaries.

3. POCSO, CPP, SPACE Model - Complete the POCSO training and write the understanding and reflection of POCSO, CPP and SPACE Model within the SC scope.

4. SC Practice Principles - Create an agreement outlining your principles, boundaries, communication practices and professional commitments for working with students as a SC.
Input / Resource: SC Training Module 2026-27; Case Studies: 01 & 02; POCSO; SC Practice Principles; school safeguarding/POCSO SOPs; discussion with TL
Measurable Criteria: Correctly identifies role scope and boundaries; makes safe confidentiality/escalation decisions; no critical safeguarding error in case scenarios
Evidence / Output: Completed case study responses; POCSO completion record; principles application notes

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Worksheet/Activity - Create a simple student-facing tool for Grades 9–12 that addresses a common student need and can be used in a 1-on-1 SC session.

2. Dummy Session - Plan, pitch and deliver a complete dummy Student Champion session for Grades 9–12, including topic selection, session planning, digital tools, promotion, team pitch, delivery, feedback analysis and reflection.
Measurable Criteria: Produces a useful activity/output; can explain guidebook expectations; runs a coherent dummy session
Evidence / Output: Completed worksheet/activity; guidebook notes; dummy session plan + reflection

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. Case Simulation - Respond to realistic student scenarios through structured action plans, focusing on student support, boundaries, stakeholder collaboration and reflection on your approach.

2. Conversation Framework - Learn and apply the SC conversation framework.

3. Understanding the Student - Build a well-rounded understanding of two students using school data, observations, student voice and evidence-based reflection, while maintaining confidentiality and avoiding assumptions or labels.

4. Student Meeting - Conduct, reflect on and reattempt a real student meeting using the conversation framework, incorporating Mentor/TL feedback to strengthen your communication, boundaries and follow-up skills.

5. Academic Accountability & Student Agency - Support a student through Analyse → Plan → Act → Follow Up → Reflect, helping them understand academic patterns, take ownership of their plan, and build independent accountability.
Input / Resource: SC Training Module 2026-27; conversation framework; Case Simulation scenarios; observed SC modelling; mentor/TL supervision
Measurable Criteria: Builds rapport, listens actively, uses appropriate questions and preserves student agency; improves after feedback; no critical error
Evidence / Output: Simulation rubrics; framework practice; observed student meeting (attempt + reattempt); reflection

Detailed Task / What the New Joinee Will:
1. P-T-S - Role-play conversations with the student, teacher and parent to practise neutral communication, confidentiality, stakeholder collaboration and appropriate escalation.

2. Teacher Communication - Practise communicating student concerns with teachers through evidence-based, respectful and collaborative conversations while maintaining student voice, confidentiality and SC boundaries.

3. Parent Communication - Practise understanding a family-related concern, collaborating with another SC, and engaging parents without comparison, while maintaining student voice, confidentiality and professional boundaries.

4. Referral Mapping Cases - Respond to three cases where student needs move beyond the SC role, focusing on recognising limits, maintaining boundaries, collaborating with WBC/CC/parents, and making appropriate referrals or escalations.

5. Case Conference - Present two student cases to relevant stakeholders using evidence, student voice and professional judgement to build a collaborative, student-owned support plan.
Input / Resource: SC Training Module 2026-27; communication protocols; Referral SOP; Refferal Mapping Cases process; case conference format
Measurable Criteria: Communicates objectively; protects confidentiality; maintains boundaries; does not overpromise/diagnose; escalates appropriately
Evidence / Output: Meeting observation forms; role-play/simulation rubrics; case conference record
